title: The good word, the good tree
hookLine: a good word is like a good tree, roots firm, branches in the sky, fruit in every season (14:24–25)
carry: a good word is a tree

lines: A BOY TOO SHY TO ANSWER.
cards: Medina. A group of companions sits with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and he gives them a riddle. There's a tree, he says, whose leaves don't fall, and it's like a believer.
What tree is it? The grown men start guessing desert trees, one after another. In the circle sits a boy, 'Abdullah, the son of 'Umar.
He thinks he knows. But he looks around at the older men, at his own father, and he's too shy to say it. Bukhari keeps the scene.
The answer is a tree, and so is today's verse.

teach.b: The answer was the date palm. Ibn 'Umar told his father afterward, and 'Umar said he'd have loved it if his son had spoken up.

teach.h: ROOTS FIRM, BRANCHES IN THE SKY.
teach.b: Now the verse, Surah Ibrahim twenty-four and twenty-five, in Pickthall's translation: "Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven, Giving its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord?"
A goodly saying: kalima tayyiba, a good word.

teach.h: LA ILAHA ILLALLAH, OR ANY GOOD WORD.
teach.b: Many commentators, following Ibn 'Abbas, say the good word is the testimony at the heart of Islam: la ilaha illallah, no god but God.
Its roots go down into the heart, its branches go up in good deeds, and it gives fruit all year. Others read it more widely: any good word, any true and kind speech. Both readings are old.

teach.h: THE BAD TREE HAS NO HOLD.
teach.b: Then verse twenty-six gives the opposite: a bad word is like a bad tree, torn up from the surface of the earth, with no hold at all.

teach.h: A GOOD WORD IS A TREE.
teach.b: A good word, once said, keeps growing. The thing a teacher said when you were twelve. The sentence from your grandmother you still repeat.
The kind remark from a stranger that got you through a week. And a bad word? It feels powerful when it's said, but it has no roots.
It blows away, though not before it does damage. A hadith in Bukhari puts it simply: a good word is charity.

how: Muslim teachers explain 14:24–26 with the date palm hadith, and many read the good word as the testimony la ilaha illallah; the hadith 'a good word is charity' is widely taught to children.

o: a polite greeting said when you meet someone
a good word, rooted firm and bearing fruit all year
a sweet-smelling tree planted near a mosque

games.q: the good tree — tap the pairs.
p: knew the answer, too shy to say

s: the young Ibn 'Umar answered the riddle first
he knew it but was too shy; 'Umar later said he wished his son had spoken.
commentators read the good word only one way
many say la ilaha illallah; others read any good, true word. both readings are old.
the good tree gives fruit in every season
its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven, giving its fruit at every season.

games.q: you're the youngest in a circle of grown men. the Prophet asks a riddle, and you know the answer. what does Ibn 'Umar do?
games.why: he stayed quiet. later his father 'Umar told him he'd have loved it if he had spoken up.

practice: Remember a good word someone once said to you that's still growing: who said it, and where were you? Let yourself be grateful for it, then think of someone tired who could use a true, kind word of yours.
If you pray, you can say la ilaha illallah, the good word as many commentators read it.

wordCard.voice: Kalima tayyiba. A good word, like a good tree: roots firm, branches in the sky, giving fruit in every season. Today's word.
